summary: Remove an inline editorial Russian query from the quoted Turoyo

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/2)

data.turoyo: kmarʕelən, hul d gbuhro, məd bahiro, kmaṣərre w gdowər aʕlayye.
data.translation: und lässt sie grasen, bis es hell wird. Wenn es hell geworden ist, schirrt er sie an und pflügt mit ihnen.

rationale: First I Infectum box; anticipated daylight endpoint contrasts with resulting bahiro in same passage.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (96/191)

data.turoyo: Ḥərre: "Kbahiro, nahər. Gnahər, manbahhe tloṯo bote mi walaye."
data.translation: Auf einmal sahen sie, daß es hell, daß es Tag geworden war. Als es Tag geworden war, hatten die Diebe drei Häuser der Stadt ausgeraubt.

rationale: First ko-Preterit box; k- plus bahiro, in contrast to unprefixed result and Infectum buhro.

data.turoyo: Məqqaṣ d komabahri ak kukwe di šmayo, haqqaṣ komabahri ar rumḥe di ʕaskar.
data.translation: So, wie die Sterne am Himmelleuchten so leuchten die Lanzen der krieg er.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell; both stars and lances shine without an object, grounding clarified intransitive gloss. Both tokens quoted once.

data.turoyo: Ayna d maḥatle əšma i Šəmšo du Ṣahro, lo ġaləṭ, komabahro, xd i šəmšo du ṣahro.
data.translation: Der, welcher sie Mondscheinehen genannt hatte, hatte keinen Fehler begangen. Sie leuchtet wie der Mondschein.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell; human luminous subject and explicit moonlight comparison, same intransitive light meaning.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (66/114)

data.turoyo: Baš šubhe d aloho mṣaḥela briṯo bahiro, ġalabe basəm.
data.translation: Durch Gottes gnädige Fügung klärte sich das Wetter auf, und es wurde hell; er wurde sehr vergnügt.

rationale: Thin I Preterit Intransitive cell; briṯo supplies a feminine weather subject.
The inherited bracelet example and 65/274 stars/lances have no illuminated object. Adds intransitive light emission to the same light meaning rather than introducing a duplicate sense.

summary: I ambient light occurs with masculine bahər and feminine bahiro. JTM 1.1/2 contrasts the Infectum gbuhro endpoint and Preterit Intransitive bahiro result; 96/191 supplies k-prefixed bahiro in ko-Preterit.

III alternates between causative illumination (inherited sun illuminating the world) and absolute shining of a bracelet, stars, lances or a girl. The added gloss documents a valency alternation already implicit in the entry.
25/11 and 84/32 bahərto are adjective-shaped feminine bright predicates/modifiers. Their semantic relevance is certain, but a productive Part act. box is withheld pending morphology review.
Inherited spelling mabharle in the bracelet quotation differs from supplied mabhalle. Both retain the same III L-suffix form; no automatic normalization is made.
Is bahərto in 25/11 and 84/32 a productive Part act. or a lexical adjective? Establish vowel pattern and relation to feminine finite bahiro before adding the box.
112/84: explain kolašto and ṣpahi in context. The inherited inline query about ṣpahi is preserved here after its removal from the Turoyo quotation.
Should absolute III shining and transitive illumination remain in one sense, as proposed, or receive editorial subsenses? Existing and new examples demonstrate both frames.
Human beauty is described through luminous comparison with moonlight, extending the light-emitting subject class; no separate figurative numbered sense is required.
